open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
open_points.text: The Required tests define CLK-002, but the only witness bindings are: "CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal]."
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its required clock-source behavior?
options: Bind CLK-002 to an existing verification check
Name a new receiving witness check that will assert CLK-002
open_points.default_guess: Add a dedicated CLK-002 verification witness covering wall-clock and elapsed-clock ownership.

open_points.subject: source-supplied timestamp representation
open_points.text: The rule requires source-supplied times to preserve "the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC", while the Required test says each time is "stored as supplied" without requiring conversion to offset-naive UTC or preservation of the instant across an offset conversion.
open_points.question: What must the test assert when a supplied timestamp carries an offset or timezone representation different from offset-naive UTC?
options: Assert conversion to offset-naive UTC while preserving the instant
Treat "stored as supplied" literally and retain or merely remove the supplied representation
Restrict accepted inputs so only an explicitly specified UTC representation can reach this test
open_points.default_guess: Assert that the stored value is offset-naive UTC representing the same instant as the supplied timestamp.

witness.initial: The fixed wall clock is 2035-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, and a snapshot publication supplies approved_at as 2026-06-01 12:00:00+02:00.
events: A service principal imports the snapshot.
The import stores the source-supplied approved_at.
outcomes: approved_at is stored as naive UTC 2026-06-01 10:00:00, preserving the supplied instant.
approved_at is stored as naive 2026-06-01 12:00:00 by treating "stored as supplied" as preserving the supplied wall fields.
witness.observer: A repository read or representation-focused verification test sees the two different stored values.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 elapsed-clock exclusivity
open_points.text: CLK-002 says the elapsed clock is read "only to measure the A25 rate-limit window" and is "never ... turned into an instant or ordered against a persisted record", but its Required tests only count the reading on a viewer-entry request, check the boundary decision, and check that no written record holds the reading.
open_points.question: What required test shows that no other portal path reads the elapsed clock and that viewer entry neither converts its reading into an instant nor compares it with persisted timestamps?
options: Exercise every operation with an elapsed-source counter and fail on any non-viewer-entry read, plus test the forbidden conversions/comparisons
Add an architectural or dependency check proving the elapsed source is reachable only from the A25 limiter, together with the viewer-entry behavior test
open_points.default_guess: Use an architectural ownership check plus the existing viewer-entry boundary test.

witness.initial: The elapsed source is instrumented, and persisted viewer data contains datetime timestamps.
events: A staff login operation reads the elapsed source for an internal measurement but does not persist the float.
A viewer-entry request reads it once for the A25 window and writes no float to a record.
outcomes: The implementation is rejected because elapsed time is used outside the A25 viewer-entry limiter.
All stated runtime tests pass because viewer entry reads once, no record stores the float, and the staff-login test has no elapsed-read assertion.
witness.observer: The State 8 verification suite distinguishes the outcomes only if the missing exclusivity check is added.
